q-54715.name: Question 2
q-54715.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14149933/assets/a0f793d5ed1860751c5e6c8b92c544d4d19ad1f07a10443f4ec3a433bcd9e958.png)

Which inequality corresponds to the highlighted region shown on the number line above?
q-54715.worked_solution:
There is a **closed** circle at $x=4,$ and the red arrow starts from $4$ and goes to the **right**. This indicates that $x$ should consist of all the values **greater than or equal to** $4.$

Therefore, the highlighted region represents $x\ge 4.$

q-159897.name: Question 3
q-159897.problem: Which of the following number lines represents the inequality $x\le 1?$
q-159897.worked_solution:
The condition $x\le 1$ implies that $x$ can be any value that is **less than or equal to ** $1.$

 To represent this on a number line:

- We draw a **closed** circle at $x=1.$

- Then, we draw an arrow starting from $1$ and going to the **left**.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14149933/assets/ace7c5f6f12ea43f2c857f77a8f2a27e29ee46bb0d8a40abb9ee7fe2804d088c.png)

q-25850.name: Question 4
q-25850.problem: Which of the following number lines represents the inequality $x\ge -2?$
q-25850.worked_solution:
The condition $x\ge -2$ implies that $x$ can be any value that is **greater than or equal to** $-2.$

 To represent this on a number line:

- We draw a **closed** circle at $x=-2.$

- Then, we draw an arrow starting from $-2$ and going to the **right**.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14149933/assets/4be757012411ef309bb4c224d874ce97741efe174395566eca760d0b37766df3.png)
